headline: The Financial Times says a market where people can trade contracts on future AI computing power is on its way.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: headline only; the CME launch mentioned in related coverage still needs regulatory approval.
importance_line: If it happens, AI companies and owners of computing capacity could agree prices for computing power ahead of time, but how the Financial Times sees this market is not known and the CME launch still needs regulatory approval.
summary: The Financial Times says a futures market in AI computing power is coming, meaning buyers and sellers would agree a price today for computing capacity delivered later. Separately, TokenPost reports that CME Group plans to launch two futures contracts tied to AI computing power on 5 October, subject to regulatory approval.
notes: FT paywall (403). Headline only for the FT piece; the second sentence comes from TokenPost (https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/26350), a different outlet, and may or may not be what the FT article discusses.
